create_document.description: Create a new document from a PandaDoc template, for the people who will sign it, with the template's variables and fields filled in. 'Send document' can follow straight after: it waits until PandaDoc has finished preparing the document, so no wait or status-check step is needed in between.
create_document.name: create_document

parameters.description: Name for the new document.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The PandaDoc template to create the document from. Pick one, or paste its ID from the template's link: app.pandadoc.com/a/#/templates/{id}.
parameters.name: template_uuid

parameters.description: Beta. The email of the person who signs, for a document with one signer, so no earlier step has to build a list of recipients. Use this or Recipients (or both: this person is added to them).
parameters.name: signer_email

parameters.description: Beta. The signer's first name.
parameters.name: signer_first_name

parameters.description: Beta. The signer's last name.
parameters.name: signer_last_name

parameters.description: Beta. The signer's role in the template, spelled as it is in the template's roles, such as 'Client' or 'Signer'. It gives them the template's fields to fill in and sign; left empty, they are only copied (CC) and sign nothing.
parameters.name: signer_role

parameters.description: Everyone who should receive the document, when there is more than one signer. Each needs an email; first_name, last_name and role are optional, and role must match one of the template's roles, such as 'Client'. For one signer, fill in the signer fields instead.
parameters.name: recipients

role.description: The role this person fills in the template, spelled as it is in the template's roles, such as 'Client'. It gives them the template's fields to fill in and sign. Without it they are only copied (CC) and sign nothing.

parameters.description: Beta. Values for the template's variables (PandaDoc tokens, written [Client.Company] in the template), by variable name without the brackets, such as {"Client.Company": "Acme Corp", "Deal.Amount": "12500"}. Each value can come from an earlier step, so no HTTP request is needed to fill them in. Variables left out keep the template's default.
parameters.name: values

parameters.description: Beta. Values to put in the template's fillable fields before it is sent, by the field's name in the template (its Field ID), such as {"Start date": "2026-12-01", "Agree": true}: true or false for a checkbox, text for the rest. Fields left out stay empty for the recipient to fill in.
parameters.name: fields

document_id.description: ID of the created document. Use with get-document-status and send-document.

document_link.description: Beta. The document's page in PandaDoc, ready for a message to the person who owns the deal, so no step has to build the address.

status.description: Document status immediately after creation, typically 'document.uploaded' while PandaDoc prepares it. 'Send document' waits for it to be ready, so there's no need to check this first.

download_document.description: Save a PandaDoc document as a PDF file, with its signatures once everyone has signed, so later steps can attach it or upload it to Drive.

parameters.description: The document to download: the id from the Document completed trigger, 'Create document from template' or 'List documents'.

list_documents_waiting_for_signature.description: List the documents (proposals, contracts, quotes) that were sent and still aren't signed, optionally only those sent more than a number of days ago or worth more than an amount. Each comes ready to tell someone about: who sent it, who still has to sign, its total, when it was sent, how many days it has waited and a link. The result also has the list written out one line per document (text), and the same grouped by who sent them (by_sender), for one reminder to each sender. It reads the whole account, so no paging, filtering, grouping or lookup steps are needed. One run looks up at most 100 documents, the longest-waiting first; 'has_more' is true when some were left for another run.

pandadoc_document_completed_trigger.description: Runs when everyone has signed a PandaDoc document, such as a proposal or contract. Documents completed before the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.client_company: Beta. That customer's company, such as Acme Corp, from the template's variable for their role (Client.Company); blank if the document doesn't say.
output.client_email: Beta. That customer's email, such as jane@acme.com.
output.client_name: Beta. The customer's name, such as Jane Doe: the first signer who isn't on your side. Someone is on your side when they created, own or sent the document, or their email is at the creator's company domain (gmail.com and other public addresses don't count). If every signer is on your side, the first signer.
output.currency: Beta. The total's currency code, such as USD.
output.grand_total: Beta. The document's total from its pricing table, as a number such as 12500.0 (0 if it has none), ready for an invoice amount.
output.grand_total_display: Beta. The total ready to read, in the document's currency, such as $12,500.00 (blank if it has no total).
output.hubspot_deal_id: Beta. The id of the HubSpot deal the document was made from or linked to in PandaDoc, such as 12345678901, ready for HubSpot's deal steps. Blank if it isn't linked to one.
output.id: The document's id, for 'Download a document'.
output.linked_objects: Beta. Every CRM record the document is linked to: a list where each has provider (such as hubspot or salesforce), entity_type (such as deal) and entity_id. Empty if none, or if PandaDoc couldn't say.
output.name: The document's name.
output.recipients: Beta. Everyone the document was for: a list where each person has name, email, company (blank if the document doesn't say), role (such as Client) and signed (true once they finished).
